requirements.statement: The notification hub's browser title is 'Overview - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and its main heading is 'Overview'.
requirements.why: The hub is the top of the notification in Design Release 2.1, named Overview.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-002 and trace-animals-fit-p4-002 show the title and h1 'Overview' today.

requirements.statement: Each live-animals notification has its own hub page in the live-animals set, keyed by the notification (today /live-animals/notifications/{reference}), rather than one hub page for whichever notification is in the session.
requirements.why: The real service stores many notifications per trader, so the hub must say which one it shows; the prototype holds a single notification in its session and cannot express this, and the prototype never decides URL paths (ruling:sam-2026-10-09).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-001 serves the hub at /notifications/{journeyId} under the live-animals set; c-128 keeps it over the prototype's single /notification-hub route.

requirements.statement: Above the 'Overview' heading the hub shows the notification's status as a tag ('Draft' until it is submitted) followed by the notification reference, which the notification already has before any task is answered, in the form 'GBN-AG-', a two-digit year, a hyphen and six upper-case letters or digits (for example GBN-AG-26-DGWJ47).
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are on and what state it is in.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-004 and trace-animals-fit-p4-003 show the journey strip with a 'Draft' tag and the reference above the heading today, and trace-animals-fit-p4-004 shows every reference already in the GBN-AG-26-XXXXXX form from the first page.

requirements.statement: Opening the hub leaves the notification saved as a draft: nothing a trader has answered is lost by leaving from the hub.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves the draft when the hub opens; the real service already saves each page's answers to the notification record as it goes.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p13-044-m1 shows every saved page committing to the stored notification (the concurrency token rises per save), so the draft is already saved whenever the hub shows.

requirements.statement: While a submitted notification is being amended (status 'Amend'), the hub's status line also shows a 'Cancel amend' link-style control, which goes to the cancel-amendment confirmation page the review page uses (a page, never a pop-up). It comes from the shared status strip, so the live-animals, germinal-products and high-risk plants Overview pages all show it, with no plants-specific work.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's shared status line offers Cancel amend on every page that includes it, and the hub's missing modal include is a prototype omission (c-127); the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the Amend bar's 'Cancel amend' going to the confirmation page, changes it in the shared strip because every set that amends needs it, and holds the pop-up back as a waiting-on-design question.
requirements.deltaNote: The real hub's strip shows only the tag and reference (repo-frontend-p4-004), as plants' does (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-076); cancel amend is offered today only from the review page and the dashboard. Built by the shared strip change (the Amend bar increment, the one change the ruling allows to the shared strip in place), which reaches every set's hub at once.

requirements.statement: The hub has no back link; the ways off it are the 'Return to dashboard' button and the service navigation.
requirements.why: The hub is the top of the notification, not a step in it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-005 and trace-animals-fit-p4-005 show no back link on the hub today.

requirements.statement: The hub shows a 'Your commodities' heading (h2) above the commodity total cards, on every visit, including before any commodity is chosen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens the hub with the consignment totals.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-006 and trace-animals-fit-p4-007 show the 'Your commodities' h2 from the first visit today.

requirements.statement: For a live-animals notification the first card shows the total number of animals, labelled 'Animals' with the caption 'Total number of animals in this consignment'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy for the animals total card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-007 and trace-animals-fit-p4-008 show the 'Animals' label and caption verbatim today.

requirements.statement: The hub shows a card for the total number of packages, labelled 'Packages/boxes' with the caption 'Total number of packages in this consignment'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy for the packages total card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-008 and trace-animals-fit-p4-009 show the 'Packages/boxes' label and caption verbatim today.

requirements.statement: The animals and packages totals add up only counts that are positive whole numbers, and a card reads '0' when its total is not above zero: commodity details refuses any number of animals or packages that is zero, negative or not a whole number, so only blank or positive counts reach the totals, and a blank count adds nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts only positive entries, so a card never shows a negative or odd total.
requirements.deltaNote: Already met: commodity details refuses a number of animals below 1 or not whole and a number of packages that is not a whole number of 1 or more (repo-frontend-p5-067, repo-frontend-p5-068, proved by trace-animals-fit-p9-050 and trace-animals-fit-p9-052), and templates are seeded from the same checked answers, so no zero, negative or non-numeric count can reach the hub. Blank counts add nothing (repo-frontend-p4-010), lines are summed (repo-frontend-p4-009) and both totals read 0 before any line exists (repo-frontend-p4-011, trace-animals-fit-p4-067). Today's arithmetic would subtract a negative count, but no path can save one, so nothing changes.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the hub's 'Your commodities' shows the 'Packages/boxes' card and a weight card labelled 'Kilograms' with the caption 'Total weight of packages in this consignment', and no 'Animals' card.
requirements.why: Germinal products are counted by packages and weight, not by animals, in Design Release 2.1; each set holds one category, so the germinal hub never mixes in an animals count.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists today, and the only hub always shows the Animals and Packages/boxes cards (trace-animals-fit-p4-008) with no weight card. Built in the germinal set's copy of the hub.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the 'Kilograms' card totals the gross weight in kilograms entered for the consignment, and shows '0' when the total is not a positive number, a whole number as entered, and otherwise the total rounded to 3 decimal places (for example '2.5').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's rule for displaying the weight total; the weight the germinal set holds is a total gross weight in kilograms, as a decimal.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set or weight card exists today.

requirements.statement: Each commodity total card is a static panel (no link or button) that reads the number, then the label, then the caption; the cards sit side by side on a wide screen and stack with no horizontal scrolling on a 360px screen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the totals as value, label and caption tiles; the real hub already draws them that way from GOV.UK design tokens.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-012 to p4-016 and trace-animals-fit-p4-014 to p4-018 show static number-label-caption panels, side by side and stacking on a small screen, today.

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks these regions up for screen-reader users.

Transport and arrival', '4. Documents', '5. Consignment parties', '6. Contact address', and nothing after them (no review task row).

Only the third row's title changes (req-794).

requirements.statement: 'Commodity details' is its own row, first in section 2, shown from a fresh notification as 'To do'; it reads 'Complete' once the number of animals (and packages where asked) is saved for every chosen commodity, while 'What are you importing?' reads 'Complete' as soon as a commodity is chosen.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-020/p4-041 and trace-animals-fit-p4-032 to p4-034 show the separate row, first in section 2, live with 'To do' from the start, as DR2.1 does (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p11-032); this settles the open DR1 gating call (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-043) as the status quo.

requirements.statement: 'Identification details' shows in section 2, between 'Commodity details' and 'Additional details', only when a chosen commodity needs animal identifiers, and is absent otherwise (for example before a commodity is chosen, or for poultry).

Which commodities carry identifiers, and what makes the row complete, belong to the animal-identification area.

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the additional animal details task for live animals; with each set holding one category, every live-animals notification owes it. The germinal half is a requirement of its own (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 13).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-035 makes only Identification details and Transit countries conditional, so 'Additional details' is always shown today (trace-e2e-p13-021, trace-animals-fit-p4-042), which is what the live-animals set needs once its catalogue holds only live animals.

requirements.statement: Section 3 always shows 'Arrival details', which opens even before a commodity is chosen, and 'Transport details'; each reads 'Complete' once its answers are saved.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-021 and trace-e2e-p13-024 show both rows in section 3 today, and trace-animals-fit-p4-044/045 show Arrival details opening and completing before a commodity is chosen.

The rule that decides when they are required belongs to the arrival-and-transit area.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-022 and trace-animals-fit-p4-050/051 show the single 'Upload documents' row, 'To do' while the rest is complete, with the review still open; trace-e2e-p13-033 shows the notification submittable without documents.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-026/p4-046 and trace-animals-fit-p4-052 to p4-054 show the row, its hint verbatim, and CPH folded into it today.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-024 and trace-animals-fit-p4-055 show the row, verbatim, completing once a contact is chosen, today.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-029 to p4-031 and trace-animals-fit-p4-024 show only green 'Complete' and blue 'To do' today.

requirements.statement: Every row the hub shows is a link the trader can open at any time, in any order: no row is locked or shown as 'Cannot start yet', and a row that does not apply is left off the hub rather than shown locked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader start any task in any order.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-027/p4-033/p4-034/p4-057 and trace-animals-fit-p4-026 show every shown row as a link, none 'Cannot start yet', and inapplicable conditional rows removed, today. This holds for the live-animals hub and the germinal copy of it; the high-risk plants Overview keeps its own gated rows, which no row of this programme changes.

requirements.statement: The hub's task list is built from the GOV.UK Task list component, one per section, with each row's status (and the Roles and addresses hint) tied to its link by aria-describedby, so a screen reader moving by links hears the task, its hint and its status.
requirements.why: The prototype's custom markup does not tie status or hint to the link, which fails screen-reader users; the GOV.UK component gives the same look and meets the accessibility regulations the real service must meet.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p4-023 and trace-e2e-p13-030-m1 show GOV.UK task lists with aria-describedby status (and hint) ids today; c-129 keeps them over the prototype's custom markup.

requirements.statement: A new notification goes from choosing the notification type to the origin page, and the first hub a trader reaches already shows 'Where is this consignment coming from?' as 'Complete'; reaching the hub ends the guided first pass through the journey.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends a new live-animals notification to the origin page first, not to the hub.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-055 and trace-animals-fit-p4-027 show a new notification held on the origin page, so the first hub has origin Complete. The prototype shows an all-'To do' hub only when its URL is typed directly, which the real per-notification hub does not need to copy.

requirements.statement: A page opened from a hub row returns to the hub on 'Save and continue', rather than carrying on into the rest of its section: the main import reason no longer goes on to Additional details, Arrival details no longer goes on to Transit countries and Transport details, and the consignment addresses page no longer goes on to the CPH number page. No marker is added to the row links to do this.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 a task opened from the hub comes back to the hub when saved, so the trader chooses what to do next; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 39 adopts this by changing only the live flow's fallback, with no ?from=hub marker.
requirements.deltaNote: Today, from the hub, Save and continue moves on through the rest of the section before returning: import reason goes on to Additional details (trace-animals-fit-p4-030), port of entry on to transit countries and transporters (trace-animals-fit-p4-046, trace-e2e-p13-041), and addresses on to the CPH number (trace-e2e-p13-041). The same change as req-1615, which the ruling names.

requirements.statement: A task page opened from the hub has a 'Back' link to the hub and ends with 'Save and continue', a secondary 'Save and return to overview' that saves and goes to the hub, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link that goes to the hub without saving.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives every task page reached from the hub these ways back to it; DR1's rule (b) already limits the three controls to pages the overview links to.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p13-037 to p13-039 and p13-043 show the Back link to the hub and the three exits on task pages today.

requirements.statement: For a notification, the hub ends with a primary 'Review and submit' button that opens the review page, always shown and active whatever the task statuses; submitting is still gated on the review page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers the review at any time and names what is outstanding there.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-050 and trace-animals-fit-p4-059 show 'Review and submit' as the primary button, opening the review page with only the origin answered, today.

requirements.statement: For a notification, the hub's secondary button is 'Return to dashboard', after 'Review and submit' in the same button group, going to the set's own notification list (the dashboard) at the set's root in the animals frontend: /live-animals for a live-animals notification, /germinal-products for a germinal one.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's way off the hub; the prototype's 'overall dashboard' becomes the set's own list, because each notification list stays in its own frontend and is reframed in place there.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-052 and trace-animals-fit-p4-061 show the secondary 'Return to dashboard' linking to the set base (/live-animals), where the set's own list is today and stays (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-089, p3-103); the germinal hub's copy links to its own set root, where the germinal list's copy is (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-104).

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-064 shows the button group holding only 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard' today.

requirements.statement: The hub has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA accessibility violations, whether it shows zero totals, a commodity with numbers owed, or non-zero totals.
requirements.why: The real service must meet the accessibility regulations; the hub already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-067/p4-068 and trace-animals-fit-p4-019 show axe passing on the hub in each state today.

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the status tag reads 'Template' and the template's name is shown beside it in place of a notification reference. The shared status strip is not changed for this: in template mode the hub switches the shared strip off and draws this header in the set's own hub template.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 reuses the hub to build a template and labels it as one; template mode walks the same journey pages as a notification, with no copied pages, so the template's hub is the set's own hub in template mode. The 9 October afternoon ruling never changes the shared strip in place except for the Amend bar: a page that needs a different header switches the strip off and draws its own. Template mode is for the animals sets only: the plants Overview gets no template mode.
requirements.deltaNote: The hub today has no template mode: its strip shows only the notification's status tag and reference (repo-frontend-p4-004).

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the task list is headed 'Template tasklist'.

requirements.statement: Each germinal-products notification has its own hub page in the germinal-products set, keyed by the notification in the same way as the live-animals hub (under /germinal-products/notifications/), a copy of the live-animals hub taken once this programme has built it, plus the germinal differences.

requirements.statement: On the germinal-products hub, assistive technology can move by region: the two total cards are regions labelled 'Packages summary' and 'Gross weight summary', and the 'Your commodities' block, the task list and each numbered section are regions named by their own heading.

requirements.statement: In the high-risk plants frontend, a page opened from a task row on the Overview returns to the Overview on 'Save and continue' once the row's own pages are done, rather than carrying on into the next row: the same fallback rule as live animals (req-808, req-1615), built in the same increment by the same flow fallback, keyed to the task row rather than the flow section, with no marker on the row links. A row made of more than one page still moves through its own pages first (commodity type to the commodities list and details, arrival status to arrival details), so arrival details opened from the Overview returns there instead of going on to the place of destination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns a task opened from the overview to the overview when it is saved, and the 9 October afternoon ruling makes that change (inc-002) reach plants in the same increment, keeping plants' multi-page task rows moving within their own row.
requirements.deltaNote: Today plants' save falls back to the next reachable page in the page's flow section and only then to the Overview, so Save and continue on arrival details goes on to the place of destination, which the opening run asks next (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-026); trace-animals-fit-p4-030 shows the shared platform doing the same on live animals.

requirements.statement: In the high-risk plants frontend, 'Save and return to overview' (exit=hub) saves what was entered and goes to the overview without refusing the page for a missing required answer (on arrival status and arrival details, a blank arrival status, date, time or place of landing), while an answer that fails its own format rule is still refused with its error: a date that is not real, a future date once arrived, a time not on the 24-hour clock, a port not on the list or a quantity that is not a whole number. 'Continue' keeps today's checks.
requirements.why: Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling makes inc-003's lenient save change plants in the same increment, with malformed answers still refused. Which blank answers 'Continue' refuses stays with EUDPA-667, which owns mandatory-to-proceed against mandatory-to-submit; this changes only the exit to the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: Today plants answers every validation failure, required-ness included, with HTTP 400 and an error summary, whichever button was pressed (plants decision d-059).

requirements.statement: On the plants Overview, assistive technology can move by region: each numbered group, its heading and its task list, is a region named by that group's heading, and the groups together sit in one task list region named 'Notification tasklist' (Welsh as a machine draft like the rest of the hub's Welsh), an accessible name only: plants gains no visible task list heading. This is built in the same increment as the live-animals hub's regions.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling makes the overview regions change (inc-098) reach plants too, with each task group and the task list in a named region; no row of this programme adds the 'Notification tasklist' heading to plants (the animals hub already has it), so plants gets the region without a new visible heading.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p2-057 renders each group as a medium heading followed by a GOV.UK task list, with no region around a group or the list today.

requirements.statement: The plants Overview's task statuses are not changed to Design Release 2.1's two tags: plants keeps 'Completed' (green), 'In progress' (light blue), 'Not yet started' (blue) and the untagged 'Optional'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: plants changes only in the same increment as an animals row that changes the same page or behaviour, and the animals hub already shows Design Release 2.1's two tags, so no row changes them; there are no separate plants increments.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants works out five task states (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-036, p2-037) and shows four of them on the Overview (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-065 to p2-068), where Design Release 2.1 shows 'Complete' and 'To do' only; no plants fit test yet covers an in-progress, completed or optional row (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-087).

requirements.statement: The plants Overview's gated rows are not opened up: a plants row none of whose pages is reachable keeps showing 'Cannot start yet' with no link, as origin, arrival, destination, consignor and identification numbers do before the commodity type is answered and contact does before origin is answered.
requirements.why: Out of scope: plants keeps its own step order, and the animals hub already lets every row open in any order, so no row of this programme changes plants' gating.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants gates rows behind 'Cannot start yet' (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-069, p2-070, proved by p2-079 to p2-081 and p2-084 to p2-086), where Design Release 2.1 opens every row at once.

requirements.statement: The plants Overview's '4. Check and submit' group, with its 'Check and submit' row that reads 'Cannot start yet' until the notification is ready, is not replaced by Design Release 2.1's always-active 'Review and submit' button.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the animals hub already ends with the 'Review and submit' button, so no row of this programme changes the overview's ending, and plants keeps its own sections. The plants half of the run-ends-on-review row reaches plants' review page from the opening run, not from the Overview.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants ends its Overview with a gated 'Check and submit' task row in its own group (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-060, p2-071) where Design Release 2.1 has a primary 'Review and submit' button.

requirements.statement: The plants Overview keeps its Back link to the dashboard; it is not removed to match Design Release 2.1's hub, which has none.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the animals hub already has no back link, so no row of this programme changes it, and there are no separate plants increments.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p2-073 and p2-077 give the plants Overview a Back link to the dashboard today.

requirements.statement: The plants Overview keeps its own groups, rows, row titles and headings, in English and Welsh: its four numbered groups ('1. About the consignment', '2. Arrival and destination', '3. Consignment parties', '4. Check and submit'; Welsh '1. Am y llwyth', '2. Cyrraedd a chyrchfan', '3. Partïon y llwyth', '4. Gwirio a chyflwyno') as medium headings with no 'Notification tasklist' heading, a group with no rows left out; its seven task rows in its own order ('What are you importing?', 'Where is this consignment coming from?', 'Arrival details', 'Place of destination', 'Consignor or exporter' shown only for plants for planting and wood and cut trees, 'Identification numbers', 'Contact address for consignment') with no hints; and no 'Your commodities' totals. The Welsh stays a machine draft, not shipped without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: Out of scope: plants keeps its own questions, sections, cards and step order when mirrored, no row of this programme changes the Overview's groups or row titles (the consignor rename changes the picker's heading, title and check-answers label only), and its provisional group headings wait on plants' own copy pass (d-069), not on this programme.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants' Overview structure (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-027, p2-057, p2-060, p2-062) differs from Design Release 2.1's live-animals hub and stays as it is.

conflicts.about: Whether the hub's 'Cancel amend' link does anything: DR2.1 shows it on the hub during an amendment but does not put the cancel-amendment modal on the hub page.

positions.says: While the status is 'Amend', the status line shows a 'Cancel amend' button that opens the cancel amendment modal.
The hub page does not include the cancel amendment modal, so the button has nothing to open there.
The prototype (Design Release 2.1) wins by default over what the real services do today.
The amend and cancel confirmations stay separate pages at today's routes, carrying the pop-up's wording as page content; pop-ups are not built.
The Amend status bar is still built, and its 'Cancel amend' goes to the cancel confirmation page.

conflicts.outcome: During an amendment the hub's status line shows 'Cancel amend', and it goes to the cancel-amendment confirmation page the review page uses. DR2.1's shared status line designs the control to open the cancel amendment modal; the hub page's missing modal include is a prototype omission, not a design intent, so the control is shown on the hub. The 9 October afternoon ruling, which ranks first, keeps the confirmation a page rather than a pop-up and builds the bar in the shared strip, so every set's hub shows it; the pop-up itself waits on design. prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-009 still backs the control being shown, so only its missing-modal companion is set aside.

conflicts.about: The hub's address: one /notification-hub page for the session's notification, or one hub per stored notification in each set.

positions.says: The prototype never decides architecture, URL paths included; germinal pages sit at /germinal-products/notifications/{journeyId}/{slug}.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides the prototype.
The hub is reached at GET /notification-hub, for the one notification held in the session.
The hub is served per notification at /notifications/{journeyId}.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings win: the real service persists many notifications per trader, which the prototype's session cannot express, and the prototype never decides URL paths. Each set keeps a per-notification hub in its own path shape: the live-animals hub as it is, and the germinal-products hub under its own set. What each hub shows still follows DR2.1.

conflicts.about: The hub task list markup: DR2.1's custom tasklist with status and hint not tied to the link, or the GOV.UK Task list component.

positions.says: Claim 6 of the 7 October ruling stands for look and feel: a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
The task list is custom app-notification-hub-* markup rather than the GOV.UK Task list component.
A task's status tag and hint are not tied to its link, so a screen reader moving by links hears only the task name.
The hub's task list is built from custom app-notification-hub-* classes rather than the GOV.UK task list component.
The hub task list is a bespoke app-notification-hub-tasklist component, not the GOV.UK Task list.
Each section is a GOV.UK Task list with the status (and hint) tied to the link by aria-describedby.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the real service must meet the public sector accessibility regulations, a constraint a prototype does not carry. The GOV.UK Task list gives the same visible rows, tags and hint as DR2.1, so the look and copy follow DR2.1 and the markup stays the GOV.UK component.

conflicts.about: How a page opened from the hub knows to return there: the prototype's ?from=hub marker on every row link and form, or the real flow's own fallback with no marker.

positions.says: No ?from=hub marker is added; only the live flow's fallback changes so overview-opened pages return to the overview.
The prototype never decides query parameter or form field names.
Each task is a link to its page with ?from=hub added, so the page knows the user came from the hub.
A task page opened from the hub carries the hub origin through the form as a hidden field from=hub.
The reason form carries the hub origin only in a hidden field, while the documents form keeps ?from=hub in its action.
Each hub task link carries ?from=hub.
Hub task links carry a from=hub query.
Re-entering an answered page from the hub and saving returns to the hub with no exit or change field in the post.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the return-to-hub behaviour is built (req-808), but by the live flow's fallback, with no from=hub query or hidden field. The prototype claims that a row opens a given page (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p11-022 to p11-031) still stand for which page each row opens; only the marker claims are overruled. trace-e2e-p13-041-m1 shows the real flow already returns without a marker on re-entry and is kept.

conflicts.about: The accessible name of the germinal hub's weight card region: DR2.1 calls it a net weight card ('Net weight summary'), but the germinal set holds a total gross weight.

positions.says: In the germinal set, weight is a total gross weight in kilograms, held as a decimal.
For germinal products the hub shows a net weight card labelled 'Kilograms' with the caption 'Total weight of packages in this consignment'.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins on what the card names: the region is labelled 'Gross weight summary', matching the gross weight the set holds (and c-022). The visible label 'Kilograms' and the caption 'Total weight of packages in this consignment' say nothing of net or gross and stay as DR2.1 shows them, so prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-013 still backs the visible card and is not overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether plants' 'Save and return to overview' refuses a page for a missing required answer

positions.says: inc-003 also changes plants: its pages with exit=hub save without required checks, but malformed answers are still refused.

Plants pages already offer 'Save and return to hub' (exit=hub), and today that exit runs the same checks as continuing (plants decision d-059: required-ness and format checks, HTTP 400 and an error summary on every failure).

conflicts.outcome: Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling outranks the plants frontend: 'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required checks and still refuses a malformed answer. repo-plantsfrontend-p2-084 is not overruled, because the exit itself, plants' format checks, its required-ness at submit and its 'Continue' behaviour all stand; which blanks 'Continue' refuses stays with EUDPA-667.

conflicts.about: Whether the high-risk plants Overview takes the Design Release 2.1 hub's look where it differs (two status tags, every row open, a 'Review and submit' button, no Back link, the hub's sections and totals) although no row of this programme changes those parts of the animals hub.

positions.says: Each hub task shows only a green 'Complete' or a blue 'To do' tag.
Every hub task is always a link: none is shown as 'Cannot start yet'.
The plants Overview works out five task states, gates rows behind 'Cannot start yet', ends with a 'Check and submit' row and keeps its own four groups and seven rows.
Rows with no plants equivalent leave the plants frontend unchanged; plants changes only in the same increment as an animals row that changes the same page.
Plants keeps its own questions, answers, sections, cards, step order and data when a change is mirrored.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling wins: plants changes only where an animals row of this programme changes the same page, and there are no separate plants increments. The live-animals hub already shows Design Release 2.1's two tags, open rows, 'Review and submit' button, missing Back link and sections, so no row changes them and the plants Overview keeps its own (req-1981 to req-1985). It does take the changes an animals hub row makes: the return to the Overview on save (req-1934), the lenient save and return (req-1935), the regions (req-1979) and the Amend bar through the shared strip (req-782). The prototype claims still back the animals hub, so nothing is overruled.
